subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw guarantee for global agent dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, direct `tools.invoke`, built-in/plugin/client tools, and hooks?
rationale: This would become a user-trusted safety boundary, and the current code has several execution surfaces where a narrow process-global adapter flag would not be sufficient.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive request-scoped mode with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Keep scoped-only dry-runs
options.body: Reject a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing, and continue improving command-specific preview paths instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive request-scoped mode with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest combination of project decision authority and feature-history ties to the agent CLI and tool adapter.
